title: Correcting the date of the Armstrong small-band session, "Miss New Orleans"
summary: He says the Jepsen date should be October 1947 and recalls modulating from E-flat to G on "The Blues Were Born in New Orleans" in a bebop way.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: You were saying, I believe, when we were looking at the Armstrong section of the discography, that they had a date wrong, a year wrong?

Yeah, they have it listed here as October 17, 1946. But it was October 17, 1947. That was the date after the picture with Louis Armstrong, the picture New Orleans, and in the band was Kid Ory, Barney Bigard, Charlie Beal, Bud Scott and myself, Minor Hall playing drums, of

course. This is where we did "Do You Know What It Means To Miss New Orleans?" This was the first recording ever of that song. And another one was "The Blues Were Born In New Orleans." That's where he named all of the guys in the band. And another one, "Mahogany Hall Stomp."
Those are listings out of the Jepsen Discography, Volume 1, 1942-1965.
So we just corrected a mistake.

Anyhow, on "The Blues Was Born in New Orleans," I remember when we were putting it together in the studio, the first part was in E-flat, then before it got to my section, we had to change keys. So changing the keys was left up to me, and all these guys were playing like Dixieland, and my thing was really Bebop. So I went from the key of E-flat to the key of G [SINGS LINE], and they were surprised, but they really didn't know what I had done. Anyhow, so all of the hipsters, the guys who were from my era, said, "Hey, you were playing Bebop with those cats." And I hadn't changed a thing. I was just playing the way I played.
